caption:
How long before you can tell whether a treatment worked?
Longer than the day you were hoping for, and it depends on what was done.

Three clocks run at once. On day one you are mostly looking at the procedure - swelling, redness, and relief that it is over. Over the following weeks and months, collagen gets built rather than delivered. And then there is the day you actually decide, which almost nobody sets in advance.

A small study followed twenty people after a tightening treatment. At one year, 95% of patients and their own physicians rated the faces as improved. A blinded assessor rated 6 of 14 evaluable subjects as improved. Twenty people, open-label, no control group - this does not show the treatment failed. It shows that a blinded stranger is a harder test than your own memory, and that how you judge changes what you conclude.

So put three dates in the diary instead of one. A photograph before anything is done. A window you agree not to judge inside. And one date to look properly, once.

General education only.

#AestheticConsultation #InformedConsent #KoreanAesthetics #MedicalAesthetics #BetterDecisions
first_comment: The part that surprises people: a plan with no verdict day quietly turns into a subscription. When did you last set a date to actually decide?

slides.alt_text: Slide 1 of 6: A shallow bowl of water on oak, its surface almost still. When can you tell if it worked?
Slide 2 of 6: Three cards - day one, the months after, the day you decide. Paying and knowing are different days.
Slide 3 of 6: Six of fourteen rated improved by a blinded assessor, where 95 percent self-rated improvement.
Slide 4 of 6: Three dates - day zero, the quiet window, the verdict day. Put three dates in the diary, not one.
Slide 5 of 6: How long before you look, by treatment type: two weeks, two weeks, one to three months, four to eight weeks.
Slide 6 of 6: Day zero, the window, the date - three questions to settle before the next appointment.
